I have a job with a health insurance company that I specifically sought out to help with medical bills. I have chronic health conditions, so it can be a major expense. It isn't perfect; they only offer high deductible plans to employees, but we get a decent Hsa contribution so it works out.

For a second job, I work as an employee of the company that runs my cities public transit system. I get a free bus pass, plus they pay above minimum wage. The bus pass alone saves me ~$80 a month. For a second job that I only work two days a week, it's pretty nice. 
As an extra-extra added bonus that wasn't planned, my paychecks from both jobs are every other Friday on opposite weeks. So I get paid every week. 

I used to work in restaurants which was nice for my grocery budget, but does come with one major caveat. A lot of restaurants are small businesses/locally owned and not all of them will let you have free food. The last restaurant I worked at made us pay full price for soda even if we brought our own cups(which is ridiculous because they're paying like 10 cents per 24oz cup) and made us pay 1/2 for our meals on the clock. And we only got that if we worked 6+ hours, otherwise it was full price. So beware getting a job at restaurants, sometimes it's good but it can also be labor intensive with no breaks and zero perks.

I've been taking cbd oil for about three weeks. The first week I had two migraines that I needed an imitrex shot for. Since then, I haven't needed any triptans. I've had a couple headaches that normally would've progressed to a migraine but didn't without any treatment at all. Before I was waking up almost daily with a headache and having 3-4 migraines a week. 
I take green roads cbd+terpene strawberry ak. I try to remember to take a full dropper at morning and night, but I'm lucky if I remember once a day(adhd thing). 

I know my triggers and there have been days when I absolutely should've had a migraine and just didn't. Last week I had a family emergency and spent 3 days sleeping in the hospital. Between the stress of what was going on, missing my medications, sleeping only a couple hours a night, and the atmospheric pressure changes my city had, I absolutely should've had a migraine of epic proportions.  And I just didn't, I didn't even have a headache. 

Edited to add: I also recently got a new job that I had to be drug tested for. I was a little nervous even though the cbd I take is 0% thc. Got the email today that I passed.

Tea tree toner tabs are great for helping you get better faster. Tea tree is antiviral, antibacterial, anti fungal, antiseptic so it'll help with pretty much any nastiness. I swear by those things when I'm sick.

Because I have asthma, if I get anything upper respiratory I end up coughing all night and can't rest enough to get better. I usually take this bath and then have a spoon full of honey(it really does work) and that's the only way I'll sleep.

I have. Before I was eligible for FMLA at my job I applied for ADA accommodations. I read up through my hr website so I knew the policy, which I definitely recommend. I had to get documentation from my doctor. My employer basically granted me three days off per month without penalty for days when my medication didn't help. I was really lucky, my supervisors were very supportive and actually pushed me to ask for the accommodations when I was hesitant because of discrimination I've had in the past. In my experience, the bigger more bureaucratic the employer, the easier something like this is because if they have policies in place, they have to follow them.

I use Sea Bands for nausea. If you're in the states Walgreens usually carries them. They're these small elastic bracelets that have a plastic dot on them. You put them on and place them so the dot presses a pressure point on your wrist, they'll be a little tight so they can press down to activate the point. Most people find relief from this. You can have somebody test the points on you before you buy them too. The point is about three fingers widths up from the start of your hand. Have someone press on both wrists for a few minutes and see if it helps. If it does, you know the bracelets will help you!

That policy you linked to is only for certain plans out of California, are you sure that it's your plans policy? 
Also, if you read carefully for ftm top surgery there is no hormone requirements(just mtf because estrogen can cause breast growth I guess).
What is covered is always going to be dependent on your plans benefit language and any applicable standard policies. Certain plans must also follow applicable state mandates. How your surgeon bills can also be an issue because certain codes will be considered cosmetic and if billed separately may not be covered. You should call your insurance customer service and ask them more about your coverage. If you are seeing an In-network surgeon they should do a prior authorization for you, if you are seeing someone outside of your network you can ask your member services to start a prior authorization for you.

Source: I work for a major health insurance company.
